story.title: Seven Dead in Stampede at Hindu Temple in Bihar, India
story.summary: A stampede at a Hindu temple in Bihar, India, resulted in the deaths of seven people and injuries to at least nineteen others. The incident occurred amid a rush of devotees, reportedly triggered by panic over rumors of an electricity pole falling on worshippers. An investigation into the circumstances surrounding the stampede is currently underway.

explore_lenses.label: What triggered the crowd crush?
explore_lenses.title: A feared electrical hazard set off panic
explore_lenses.summary: Early accounts point to panic after an electrical problem outside Ashok Dham, followed by a crowd surge and collapsed barricades. Officials have not established the exact sequence or whether anyone was electrocuted.

claims.text: Civil official Shailendra Kumar said preliminary reports indicated that an electric wire snapped outside the temple at about 6:30 a.m., prompting devotees to flee a feared electrocution risk.
Kumar said barricades collapsed under the weight of the surging crowd, after which people fell over one another in the crush.
Senior police officer Shivam Kumar said reports that a pole fell and people were electrocuted still required verification before authorities could state the cause definitively.

Senior police officer Shivam Kumar said reports that a pole fell and people were electrocuted still required verification before authorities could state the cause definitively.

explore_lenses.label: Why was the temple so crowded that morning?
explore_lenses.title: The crash came during a major Shiva observance
explore_lenses.summary: The stampede occurred on the third Monday of Shravan, when large numbers of Shiva devotees make temple visits. Ashok Dham itself is identified by Bihar Tourism as a Shiva temple that draws especially large crowds during Sawan.

claims.text: Thousands had gathered near Ashok Dham to pray on the third Monday of Shravan, a period dedicated to worship of Shiva that usually falls in July and August.
Bihar Tourism says Ashok Dham is a Shiva temple where devotees gather in large numbers during Sawan and Shivaratri.
Ashok Dham also had a reported crowd-crush incident during Sawan in August 2019, when one person died and several were injured; police at the time investigated the cause.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next for victims and investigators?
explore_lenses.title: Treatment and a cause investigation are underway
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate response is hospital treatment for the injured and an investigation into the incident. Bihar's chief minister said the administration had been instructed to ensure prompt care, but no publicly documented finding on responsibility or safety failures was available in the reporting reviewed.

claims.text: More than a dozen injured people were taken to a government hospital, according to civil official Shailendra Kumar.
Kumar said the cause of the stampede was still under investigation.
Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said the administration had received instructions to provide proper and prompt treatment to those injured.

story_report.summary: Seven people were killed and at least 19 injured in a crowd crush at a Hindu temple in Bihar after panic spread among devotees during a large religious gathering. Preliminary accounts linked the rush to fears involving electrical infrastructure outside the temple, but officials had not established a definitive cause. More than a dozen injured people were taken to a government hospital, and authorities said they were investigating the circumstances.

sections.heading: Conflicting Accounts of the Crush
sections.body: Civil official Shailendra Kumar said preliminary reports indicated that an electric wire snapped outside the temple at about 6:30 a.m., causing devotees to flee over a feared risk of electrocution. He said barricades then collapsed under the pressure of the surging crowd and people fell over one another. A senior police officer said reports that a pole had fallen and people were electrocuted still required verification before authorities could determine the cause.

sections.heading: Ashok Dham Draws Seasonal Crowds
sections.body: Thousands of people had gathered near Ashok Dham to pray on the third Monday of Shravan, a period devoted to Shiva worship that usually falls in July and August. Bihar Tourism describes Ashok Dham as a Shiva temple that draws large numbers of devotees during Sawan and Shivaratri. The site also recorded a crowd-crush incident during Sawan in August 2019, when one person died and several others were injured.

unresolved.text: Authorities had not confirmed whether the initial trigger was a fallen pole or a snapped wire, whether any electrocution occurred, or the final sequence of events that caused the crowd crush.
No official investigative report, attribution of responsibility, or corrective measures had been identified in the consulted reporting as of August 17.

related_stories.title: Indonesia Earthquake Causes Deaths and Displacement Amid Ongoing Aftershocks
related_stories.summary: A powerful earthquake struck Indonesia, resulting in at least 68 confirmed deaths and thousands displaced. The earthquake, which had magnitudes of 7.7 and 6.4, triggered nearly 1,600 aftershocks, complicating rescue efforts. Many survivors are awaiting aid as search and rescue operations continue in the affected areas, particularly on Flores island, where significant damage to homes and public buildings has been reported.

related_stories.title: Death Toll from Zimbabwe Boat Capsizing Rises to 80
related_stories.summary: The death toll from a ferry capsizing on Lake Kariba, Zimbabwe, has risen to 80, with more bodies recovered. The incident occurred earlier this week, and investigations indicate that the ferry was overloaded during heavy winds. Among the deceased are eighteen children.

related_stories.title: Hayden Panettiere, actress known for 'Nashville' and 'Heroes,' dies at 36
related_stories.summary: Hayden Panettiere, the American actress famous for her roles in the TV series 'Nashville' and 'Heroes,' has died at the age of 36. Her father announced her death in a statement. The cause of death has not been disclosed, and police are reportedly investigating the circumstances surrounding her passing after she was found unresponsive at her home in South Carolina.
